name: Combinatorial Eluder Dimension of Blockwise-Addressing
details: For the displayed blockwise-addressing incidence construction.
proof: Take $f_i$ as base.  List the primary coordinates $x_j$ for $j\ne i$, witnessed by $f_j$, followed by all $y_j$, witnessed by $g_j$.  Each witness is zero at earlier listed coordinates and differs from $f_i$ at its own coordinate.  This gives $(2^d-1)+2^d=2^{d+1}-1$ steps.  The class has $2^{d+1}$ hypotheses, so the size bound is tight.
